name: Moonlight
description: Stream games from your PC with native-resolution support. Rebuilt Apostrophe wrapper with the bundled spruce moonlight-embedded engine; pair, manage servers, and launch streams from a native NextUI interface.
author: 4fuu (wrapper originally by richieszemeredi)

changelog.v0.3.6: Exit to desktop during a stream now really ends the stream. The spawned engine now sets PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL), so if the wrapper dies before its cleanup runs - the launch parent's SIGKILL escalation at the end of its exit grace, a crash, or a power path - the kernel kills the engine instead of leaving it streaming behind the desktop in its own process group. The wrapper's graceful engine stop is capped at 1 s instead of 2.5 s so it finishes inside NextUI's 1500 ms launch-parent grace, and the child restores the inherited signal mask before exec (the wrapper blocks the termination signals across fork() and the engine was starting with SIGTERM blocked). test_stream_spawn now also runs a native fake engine (a shell script clears an inherited mask) and asserts the engine starts with SIGTERM unblocked, exits on the wrapper's SIGTERM inside the grace, and dies when the wrapper is SIGKILLed.
changelog.v0.3.5: Stop the engine on every wrapper exit path. The spawned engine is registered process-wide; normal stream end, the overlay Exit action, atexit (including exit(0) from a widget/power path) and SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP/SIGQUIT all send SIGTERM to the engine process group, wait up to 2.5 s for the engine's graceful shutdown, then SIGKILL and reap. The overlay Exit action now sets the same quit flag ml_stream polls instead of unwinding past the child cleanup, and the vendored host adapter leaves the quit decision to the app. Engine config files are now written as key = value (moonlight-embedded's format) while the loader still accepts legacy key=value; streaming resolution remains argv-authoritative.
changelog.v0.3.4: Fix the libnsl ABI regression from v0.3.3: the standalone libnsl2 build does not export yp_get_default_domain@GLIBC_2.17, so libwrap failed before main. The pak now uses focal libc6's libnsl.so.1 (the same file the spruce package ships) and drops the unneeded libtirpc/Kerberos tail. CI dry-runs bin/moonlight under qemu-user against the device sysroot, so a symbol-version mismatch fails the build.
changelog.v0.3.3: Restore the complete engine library closure: 21 second-level dependencies were missing from v0.3.2 (libpulsecommon-13.99, the PulseAudio audio tail, xcb/X11, libnsl and its Kerberos tail), so bin/moonlight could not start on device. The pak now bundles all 43 non-system libraries. make-pak and CI resolve every NEEDED entry and fail on anything unresolved.
changelog.v0.3.2: Cooperation client updated to nextui-app-sdk 27e5597 (request/event lock split; a slow or blocked request can no longer stop the event stream). The in-process HOME panel now keeps polling its own input while it owns the frame, so HOME opens and closes it and the buttons work; previously the bridge stopped calling the host poll once the panel was up. overlay.state is re-queued after a timeout so devserv cannot keep a stale open/closed view.
changelog.v0.3.1: HOME is stable again: the app yields overlay hosting by default, so NextUI's system panel handles HOME/HUD while sleep inhibit, battery/status and the SDK event channel stay active. In-process hosting is opt-in (MOONLIGHT_INPROCESS_OVERLAY=1) with step-by-step logs and a 2 s open watchdog; the overlay state report no longer blocks the UI thread and the SDK event wakes an idle widget loop. Apostrophe's own power handler is disabled, so keymon owns KEY_POWER and the sleep handshake instead of the pak running suspend/poweroff directly.
changelog.v0.3.0: Cooperation layer: in-process full-fidelity HOME panel, dynamic overlay ownership (menu app / streaming system fallback), volume/brightness HUD, sleep inhibit while streaming, SDK battery/status rows.
changelog.v0.2.0: Self-contained fork: Apostrophe host seam, bundled spruce 2.7.0 engine and libs, C3 session launch, controlled stream spawn for the cooperation SDK, and the vendored full-fidelity NextUI overlay renderer.
